experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacan, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon, and explore the Avenue of the Dead. On the way back, stop at a roadside tlayuda or barbacoa stall for an authentic local lunch.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from Mexico City)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Wander the cobblestone streets of bohemian Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse artisan crafts at the local market, and sip a traditional atole or hot chocolate at a neighborhood café.

experiences.name: Tacos & Mezcal Evening in Roma Norte

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walk
experiences.description: Admire the stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture of the Palacio de Bellas Artes, view the famous Diego Rivera murals inside, then stroll through the Zócalo, explore the Metropolitan Cathedral, and visit the Templo Mayor ruins.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to hotel in Centro Histórico via Metro Line 5 to Pantitlán, then transfer to Line 2 toward Tasqueña, exit at Zócalo station (budget-friendly ~$0.30 USD fare). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), Mexico City's iconic main square. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral (free entry) and the National Palace facade with Diego Rivera's famous murals visible from the courtyard (free). Stroll along Madero Street, a pedestrian-only avenue lined with colonial architecture just steps from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the illuminated Zócalo at dusk — the square is magical as the lights come on. Head to nearby Calle Uruguay or Mesones for a casual evening walk through the historic streets.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and pan dulce at a local panadería near the hotel for under $1 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a fondita (family-run lunch spot) near the Zócalo — look for a comida corrida (set lunch menu with soup, main dish, and agua fresca) for around $3–5 USD. Try Fonda El Refugio on nearby streets.
meals.dinner: Tacos at a street taco stand near República de Uruguay — order tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor for $0.50–$1 each. Budget around $3–5 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: Keep pesos handy for street food and Metro. Exchange currency at a casa de cambio near the airport or hotel rather than airport kiosks for better rates. Stay aware of your surroundings as you settle in.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Templo Mayor (entry ~$4 USD), the ancient Aztec temple ruins located just behind the Metropolitan Cathedral. The on-site museum is included in the ticket and houses extraordinary pre-Columbian artifacts. Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Afterward, peek into the courtyard of the National Palace to see Diego Rivera's sweeping murals depicting Mexican history — entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Mercado de San Juan (~15-minute walk from the Zócalo), a beloved indoor market known for local produce, cheeses, meats, and international ingredients. Browse the stalls and sample snacks. Then head to the nearby Palacio de Bellas Artes (exterior and ground floor free) to admire the stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and check out the murals inside by Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Avenida Juárez and Alameda Central park, a beautiful public green space. Enjoy the evening atmosphere with locals. End the night exploring the lit-up streets of the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the hotel — chilaquiles or huevos rancheros with coffee for $3–5 USD. Look for places with handwritten menus for the best value.
meals.lunch: Eat inside Mercado de San Juan at one of the market stalls — try a torta, tostadas, or a fresh juice combo for $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Tacos de guisado from a street cart near Alameda Central — choose from stewed fillings like rajas con crema, picadillo, or frijoles. Around $3–4 USD for a satisfying meal.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — if this falls on a Monday, swap with Day 3 activities. Bring a reusable water bottle; purified water refills are available cheaply throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro Line 2 to Bellas Artes, then Line 3 to Tlatelolco station to visit the Plaza de las Tres Culturas in Tlatelolco (free). This powerful site blends Aztec ruins, a colonial Spanish church, and modern architecture — a symbol of Mexico's layered history. The Memorial del 68 museum nearby (free) commemorates the 1968 student massacre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the vibrant neighborhood of Tepito or loop back via Metro to explore Barrio Chino (Mexico City's small but lively Chinatown near Eje Central) before walking through the streets of Centro. Visit the Museo de la Ciudad de México (entry ~$1 USD) on Calle Pino Suárez to learn about the city's urban history housed in a beautiful colonial palace.
day_by_day.evening: Join locals at the Zócalo for evening activities — there are often free cultural events, concerts, or art installations in the square. Check local listings for free events at Bellas Artes or community theaters in the area.

meals.breakfast: Tamales and atole from a street vendor near the Metro station — a classic Mexico City morning combo for under $2 USD.
meals.lunch: Comida corrida at a local fondita near Tlatelolco or back in Centro — three courses including agua fresca for $4–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Tortas from a torta stand in Centro — try a torta de milanesa or cubana loaded with toppings for $2–3 USD. Add an agua fresca from a nearby stand.

day_by_day.notes: Tlatelolco is historically significant and emotionally impactful — allow time to reflect. The Metro is the fastest and cheapest way to get around (~$0.30 per ride). Avoid rush hours (8–9 AM and 6–8 PM) if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán, the ancient pyramids (~50 km from the city). From Centro Histórico, take Metro Line 3 to Autobuses del Norte station, then catch a bus from the Terminal Central del Norte (buses depart frequently, ~$3 USD round trip, 1-hour ride). Arrive early to climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon before midday heat. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcóatl at Teotihuacán. Browse artisan stalls outside the site for handmade crafts (practice bargaining). Head back to Mexico City by 4–5 PM via return bus to Norte station, then Metro back to Centro.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in the evening after the big day out. Take a slow walk through the illuminated streets of Centro Histórico and enjoy the nighttime atmosphere around the Zócalo and surrounding calles.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast near the Metro before departing — a quesadilla or tlacoyo from a street comal for $1–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the affordable restaurants just outside the Teotihuacán archaeological site — look for a set lunch menu (comida corrida) featuring local dishes like tlayudas or enchiladas for $4–6 USD. Avoid the overpriced tourist restaurants at the main entrance.
meals.dinner: Return to Centro and enjoy pozole or sopa de lima at a local market stall or small restaurant — warming and filling for $4–5 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes and sunscreen for Teotihuacán — it involves significant walking and climbing on exposed terrain. Bring a hat and water. Start the day by 8:00 AM to maximize time at the ruins and avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced, one of the largest and most authentic markets in Latin America, just a short walk or Metro ride from Centro Histórico (Line 1, La Merced station). Wander the vast stalls selling spices, dried chiles, herbs, street food, and everyday goods. It's a raw, real slice of Mexico City life — perfect for food lovers and culture seekers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Centro and visit the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) on Calle Tacuba (entry ~$3 USD, free on Sundays) to see Mexican fine art spanning four centuries. Afterward, take a final stroll through the streets of Centro Histórico — visit the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela (~15-minute walk) for affordable handmade souvenirs like talavera, textiles, and silver jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your last night with a proper sit-down meal at a local Mexican restaurant in Centro — splurge slightly within budget on a full meal with mole, chiles en nogada (seasonal), or enchiladas verdes. End with a mezcal or horchata at a nearby cantina.

meals.breakfast: Full Mexican breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — eggs, beans, salsa, and tortillas with coffee for $3–5 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat inside Mercado de la Merced at a market comedor — fresh-made food cooked to order including soups, stews, and antojitos for $3–4 USD.
meals.dinner: Budget splurge dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant in Centro Histórico — aim for $8–12 USD for a full meal with a drink. Try El Cardenal (known for traditional Mexican cuisine and reasonable prices) or a similar local institution.

day_by_day.notes: La Merced market is very busy and bustling — keep bags secure and enjoy the energy. Sunday is a great day for free museum entry at MUNAL. Use any remaining pesos on street food, snacks, or small souvenirs before departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the Catedral Metropolitana (free entry to the exterior and main nave) and admire the colonial architecture. Stroll along Madero Street, a pedestrian boulevard lined with historic buildings, shops, and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the illuminated Zócalo at dusk — the square transforms beautifully after dark. Head to a nearby cantina or local restaurant for your first taste of Mexican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Café de Tacuba — a historic restaurant just steps from the Zócalo serving traditional Mexican dishes like enchiladas and tamales at mid-range prices (around 150–250 MXN per dish).
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Centro branch) — a beloved local institution known for authentic Mexican cuisine, mole dishes, and house-made tortillas. Expect to spend 300–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light for the afternoon walk. Metro Line 2 (Zócalo station) is right at the square if needed. Exchange some cash at the airport or a nearby bank for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo del Templo Mayor, located just behind the Catedral Metropolitana. This archaeological site reveals the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán and includes an excellent museum with artifacts. Entry is approximately 85 MXN. Arrive early (opens at 9:00) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio Nacional on the eastern side of the Zócalo to see Diego Rivera's stunning murals depicting Mexican history — entry is free. Afterward, explore the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela, a large crafts market about 15 minutes away by metro (Line 1, Balderas station), ideal for browsing local handicrafts, textiles, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) area or wander the lit-up streets around República de Uruguay for a vibrant evening atmosphere. Consider a mezcal tasting at a local mezcalería.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café — try a traditional Mexican breakfast of chilaquiles or enfrijoladas at Hostería de Santo Domingo, one of the oldest restaurants in Mexico City (around 120–200 MXN).
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan (10-minute walk from the Zócalo) — a gourmet market with food stalls offering fresh tacos, tortas, seafood tostadas, and international bites. Budget 100–180 MXN.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — a courtyard restaurant in Centro serving refined Mexican regional cuisine in a beautiful colonial setting. Mid-range pricing around 250–450 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Palacio Nacional is free but may require a short queue. Wear comfortable shoes — today involves significant walking on cobblestone streets. Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — take an early bus from the Terminal del Norte (accessible via Metro Line 5, Terminal del Norte station) for about 52 MXN each way. Buses depart frequently from 7:00 AM. Explore the Avenue of the Dead, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon. Entry to the site is approximately 90 MXN.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl and the Palace of Quetzalpapálotl. Browse artisan vendors near the site selling obsidian crafts and local goods. Head back to Mexico City by 16:00–17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at the hotel, then head out for a calm evening stroll through the lit streets of Centro Histórico. Visit the Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles), a stunning 18th-century building now housing a Sanborns restaurant and café.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before departure — grab fresh pan dulce (sweet bread) and coffee from a street vendor or corner bakery near the hotel (30–60 MXN).
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the restaurants near the Teotihuacán site entrance — La Gruta restaurant is a unique option set inside a natural cave (300–500 MXN per person), or opt for the more budget-friendly food stalls outside the gates (80–150 MXN).
meals.dinner: Sanborns at Casa de los Azulejos — a classic Mexico City experience with solid traditional Mexican dishes in a stunning tiled interior. Around 150–280 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen and a hat — Teotihuacán is at high altitude with strong sun exposure. Bring water and snacks. Start early (by 8:00 AM) to avoid midday heat and crowds. The site is expansive; comfortable walking shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 3) to Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most charming and bohemian neighborhoods. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul / The Blue House) — book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly (entry around 270 MXN). Explore the museum's art, personal belongings, and lush garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo in the heart of Coyoacán — a lively square with street performers and artisan vendors. Visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for local snacks and shopping. If time allows, stop by the Museo León Trotsky (entry ~50 MXN), the former home of the exiled Russian revolutionary.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico or explore the nearby Colonia Roma neighborhood (accessible via Metro Line 1, Insurgentes station) for its trendy café and restaurant scene, street art, and Art Deco architecture.

meals.breakfast: Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — a legendary local coffee spot with excellent café de olla (traditional spiced coffee) and light snacks. Very affordable at 30–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: Tostadas Coyoacán at Mercado de Coyoacán — famous for their tostadas topped with tinga, seafood, or beans. A local favorite at 40–80 MXN per tostada.
meals.dinner: Contramar (Colonia Roma) — a celebrated Mexico City seafood restaurant known for its tuna tostadas and grilled fish. Mid-range at 300–500 MXN per person. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets must be booked online well in advance — check the official website. Coyoacán is about 40 minutes from Centro by Metro. The neighborhood is very walkable and safe for tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in Latin America, housing an extraordinary collection of pre-Columbian artifacts including the Aztec Sun Stone. Entry is approximately 85 MXN. Allow 2–3 hours minimum. Take Metro Line 1 to Auditorio station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest), a massive urban park and a favorite among locals. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Castle), which offers panoramic views of the city and houses the Museo Nacional de Historia (entry ~85 MXN). Explore the Paseo de la Reforma boulevard on your way back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening. Browse the souvenir shops along Moneda Street, pick up last-minute gifts, and enjoy a farewell dinner at a restaurant that best captured your Mexico City experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café in Centro — try Café de la Parroquia or any neighborhood fonda (family-run eatery) for huevos rancheros or molletes (100–160 MXN).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Chapultepec — visit the food stalls and fondas along the park perimeter for affordable tacos, quesadillas, and aguas frescas (60–120 MXN), or dine at a restaurant on Presidente Masaryk Avenue for a slightly elevated experience.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Los Girasoles in Centro Histórico — a refined yet accessible restaurant serving creative takes on traditional Mexican cuisine with a beautiful colonial dining room. Budget 300–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Anthropology Museum is massive — prioritize the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya rooms if time is limited. Chapultepec Park is very popular on weekends and can be crowded. Both the museum and castle are closed on Mondays. Confirm departure logistics for the following day.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via private luxury transfer. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of Centro Histórico: explore the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), admire the imposing Metropolitan Cathedral, and visit the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's legendary murals depicting Mexican history. Stroll through the historic streets with your expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset visit to the rooftop terrace of a nearby landmark building for panoramic views of the illuminated Zócalo. Followed by a leisurely evening walk through the lit-up historic center.

meals.lunch: Late welcome lunch at Azul Histórico, a refined Mexican restaurant set in a beautiful courtyard garden in Centro Histórico, known for regional dishes and artisanal mezcals.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Limosneros, a celebrated fine-dining restaurant steps from the hotel, offering contemporary Mexican cuisine with pre-Hispanic ingredients, paired with an extensive mezcal and wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 begins post-arrival. Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the hotel concierge. Confirm rooftop access in advance as some venues require reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum. Discover the ancient Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán beneath modern Mexico City, with expert commentary on Mexica culture, cosmology, and artifacts including the iconic Coyolxauhqui stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Palacio de Bellas Artes — Mexico's premier cultural palace — to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and the famous murals by Rivera, Orozco, Siqueiros, and Tamayo. Afterward, stroll through Alameda Central park, the oldest public park in the Americas.
day_by_day.evening: Curated mezcal and tequila tasting experience at a private mezcalería in Centro Histórico, guided by a certified spirits sommelier. Learn the craft behind Mexico's most iconic spirits paired with artisanal botanas (small bites).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café de Tacuba, one of Mexico City's most storied restaurants (est. 1912), famous for its traditional Mexican breakfast dishes and stunning Talavera-tiled interiors.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Cardenal, an institution for traditional Mexican cuisine in Centro Histórico, renowned for its handmade tortillas, mole, and classic dishes using heirloom ingredients.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol (reservation essential), ranked among the world's top restaurants. Chef Enrique Olvera's tasting menu reinterprets Mexican culinary heritage with extraordinary precision and creativity. Note: Located in Polanco — a 20-minute private transfer from the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Book Pujol well in advance — reservations are highly competitive. Arrange private car service for the evening in Polanco.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Teotihuacán, the ancient city of the gods, just 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Arrive early via private chauffeured vehicle to beat the crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead with a private archaeologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán, including the Temple of the Feathered Serpent (Quetzalcóatl) and the Palace of Quetzalpapálotl. Optional: private hot air balloon flight over the ruins at dawn (if rescheduled to early morning departure). Return to hotel by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Centro Histórico — explore the vibrant Calle Regina pedestrian street, browse artisan shops, and enjoy the neighborhood's bohemian atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Teotihuacán.
meals.lunch: Exclusive lunch at La Gruta, a spectacular restaurant built inside a natural cave (grotto) near the Teotihuacán ruins, serving traditional Mexican cuisine in an unforgettable setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar (a 15-minute transfer to Colonia Roma), Mexico City's most beloved seafood restaurant, famous for its tuna tostadas and whole grilled fish. Lively, elegant, and quintessentially chilango.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán by 8:00 AM to enjoy cooler temperatures and smaller crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sunscreen. Private guide and vehicle highly recommended for this excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in the world. Explore its extraordinary collections of Aztec, Maya, Olmec, and other Mesoamerican civilizations, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's magnificent urban forest. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec), a hilltop palace with sweeping city views and fascinating exhibits on Mexican imperial and presidential history.
day_by_day.evening: Private street food and market tour of Centro Histórico led by a local culinary expert. Visit Mercado San Juan for gourmet local products, taste authentic tacos, tlayudas, tamales, and elotes from curated street vendors, and learn the stories behind Mexico City's vibrant food culture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel's in-house restaurant or a boutique café in Centro Histórico.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quintonil, ranked among Latin America's best restaurants. Chef Jorge Vallejo's menu celebrates Mexican biodiversity and seasonal ingredients in a refined, intimate setting in Polanco (20-minute private transfer).
meals.dinner: The street food tour serves as the evening dining experience — a curated progression of Mexico City's finest street bites, elevated by expert curation and storytelling.

day_by_day.notes: The Anthropology Museum requires at least 3 hours to appreciate properly. Arrange private car for the Chapultepec and Polanco segments. The evening street food tour should be booked through a premium culinary tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Museo Dolores Olmedo in Xochimilco (or the Frida Kahlo Museum — La Casa Azul — in Coyoacán, depending on preference). Explore the life and art of Frida Kahlo in her iconic Blue House, with a private guide providing deep cultural and biographical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Xochimilco experience: board a private trajinera (flower-decorated canal boat) for a leisurely cruise through the ancient Aztec canals of Xochimilco, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Enjoy live marimba music, artisan vendors on passing boats, and the serene chinampas (floating gardens).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Centro Histórico — a final sunset stroll through the Zócalo and surrounding streets, souvenir shopping at curated artisan boutiques, and a memorable last dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely farewell breakfast at the hotel — request a special spread from the concierge to mark the final morning.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Bajío (Coyoacán branch), celebrated chef Carmen Titita Ramírez Degollado's legendary restaurant, widely regarded as one of the finest expressions of traditional Mexican regional cooking in the country.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dulce Patria, chef Martha Ortiz's visually stunning and emotionally evocative fine-dining restaurant, where Mexican folklore and femininity inspire every dish. Located in Polanco — private transfer arranged by concierge.

day_by_day.notes: La Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum) requires advance tickets — book through the hotel concierge. The Xochimilco trajinera experience is best in the afternoon. Confirm departure logistics with the hotel for the following day if flying out on Day 6.
